## Which UBC Building Are You?

*Flowchart by Selena*

[Embedded content: CC BY](https://h5p.open.ubc.ca/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=h5p_embed&id=8574)

## What Your First\-Year Residence Says About You\!

*Written by Manavi*

### Orchard Commons \(OC\)

If you live in OC, you’re an independent person who appreciates the finer things in life\. You have an eye for the newest technology and can spend hours people\-watching in Open\-Kitchen \(while enjoying the delicious egg tarts\!\)\. You love your alone time and a gorgeous sunset from the top\-floor lounge\.

### Place Vanier

If you live in Place Vanier, you’re an old soul that loves making friends and appreciates the more rustic things in life\. You’re a foodie that always tries to convince your friends to grab lunch at Vanier\. You enjoy long walks \(especially to visit your friends in OC and Totem\) and are rarely late to class, because everything is so nearby\!

### **Totem Park**

If you live in Totem Park, you’re an ambivert that enjoys spending time with yourself but also with others\. You have a calm and grounding energy that your friends appreciate, especially when you give them advice over the Honey Chicken Sesame Salad at Feast during lunch\. You’ve decorated your room, especially your accent wall, with posters of niche albums you love\!

### Ritsumeikan House

If you are one of the handful of first\-years living at Rits, you’re extremely mature and put\-together\. You value your own space and enjoy cooking your own meals instead of relying on the Dining Hall\. You really enjoy spending time with your roomates and often host movie nights\.

## Dorm Essentials

*List by Aurora*

🧹 **Hand vacuum** – grabbing the rez vacuum can be tedious

🔌 **Extension cord** – there’s never enough outlets in a dorm\!

🗑 **Mini trash can** \(with a lid\)

🧺 **Lots and lots of storage for under the bed\!**

🪭 **Compact fan** – dorm rooms can get stuffy real fast

💨 **Steamer** – a lot more compact than an iron and a board

🛀🏻 **Shower caddy**

🧦 **Laundry basket** – for storing and toting to the laundry room

🧊 **Water bottle** – make sure you get one that keeps liquids both hot and cold

## Dorm Food Recipes – No Kitchen Needed\!

*Written by Selena*

### 🌮 Single\-Serve Nachos

**Ingredients**:

-   15 tortilla chips
-   1/4 cup shredded cheese
-   1/4 avocado cubed
-   jalapeno slices, as desired
-   sliced green onions, as desired
-   cilantro roughly chopped
-   2 tbsp salsa
-   2 tbsp sour cream

**Instructions:**

1.  Arrange chips into an even layer on a microwave\-safe plate\. Layer the cheese, jalapeno slices, and green onion evenly over the chips\.
2.  Microwave until the cheese is melted \(around 1 minute\)\.
3.  Top with avocado cubes, salsa, sour cream, and cilantro\.

### 🥙 Tuna Salad Wrap

**Ingredients**:

-   2\.5 oz\. can water\-packed tuna \(drained\)
-   2 tbsp mayo
-   1 tbsp finely diced onions
-   0\.25 cup finely sliced lettuce
-   1/4 tsp salt
-   1 standard whole grain tortilla

**Instructions:**

1.  Mix the tuna, mayo, onions, and salt in a bowl until well combined\.
2.  Lay out the tortilla and put down an even layer of lettuce\. Spread the tuna salad over that\.
3.  Roll up the wrap tightly and cut in half before serving\.

### 🫐 Blueberry French Toast in a Mug

**Ingredients**:

-   1 slice of bread
-   1 egg
-   2 tbsp milk
-   ¼ tsp cinnamon
-   ½ tsp vanilla extract
-   blueberries, to taste
-   maple syrup

**Instructions:**

1.  In a bowl, mix egg, milk, cinnamon, and vanilla\.
2.  Slice the bread into cubes and add to a microwave\-safe mug with blueberries\.
3.  Pour the egg mixture into the mug\.
4.  Microwave until egg is fully cooked \(around 1\.5 mins\)\.
5.  Top with maple syrup\.

title: Dorm Essentials: What I Actually Use vs. What I Didn’t Need
content_markdown:
Before I moved into my first\-year dorm, I went on a full Pinterest\-fueled shopping spree\. I had a list, a colour scheme, and a vision and I was convinced I needed every single item the “dorm essentials” videos told me to buy\. But now as a fourth year, I am ashamed to admit that a lot of the stuff I bought is now collecting dust under my bed, while a few cheap, “un\-pretty” items have genuinely made my life easier\.

Here is what I actually use almost every day, and what I really wish I had not bought\.

## **What I actually use\!**

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-edited-1.png)

[Image from Sterilite](https://www.sterilite.com/product/6-qt-stacking-drawer/)

### Storage bins under the bed

Dorms are tiny, and the space under your bed is real estate you should absolutely be using\. I keep extra bedding, out\-of\-season clothes, and snacks in flat storage bins, and it keeps my room from feeling cluttered when there is nowhere else to put my stuff\. The bins were one of the cheapest things I bought and probably one of the most useful\.

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-1-edited.png)

[Kit](https://unsplash.com/photos/white-and-black-power-strip-YrdSQ_1gYRE) Unsplash

### A good power strip

There are never enough outlets in a dorm room\. A solid power strip with a few USB ports built in saved me from constantly fighting my roommate for the one accessible plug near my bed\. Spend a little extra on one with surge protection, because your laptop will thank you\!

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-2-940x627.png)

[Neakasa](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-woman-is-holding-a-dryer-and-ironing-clothes-ELnyS2wG3ss) Unsplash

### A steamer \(or pro tip: wrinkle release spray\)

I brought a full iron and ironing board and used them maybe twice\. A small handheld steamer is so much faster, takes up way less space, and works for basically any fabric\. And honestly, if you do not even want to deal with that, wrinkle release spray is a game changer\. You spray it on, smooth out the fabric with your hands, and walk out the door\.

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-3-940x627.png)

[Bluewater Sweden](https://unsplash.com/photos/black-and-white-plastic-containers-on-brown-sand-tF9iUErZXWA) Unsplash

### A reusable water bottle that keeps water hot or cold

I know everyone says to bring a water bottle, but I want to be a little specific here\. Get one that is properly insulated and that you actually like, because that is what determines whether you carry it around or not\. I went through three random ones before I found one that kept my water cold for hours and survived being thrown into my backpack\. It also doubles as a tea or coffee container\.

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-4-edited.png)

[Chandan Chaurasia](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-pink-fan-sitting-on-top-of-a-table-ZBa8Jp411kY) Unsplash

### A small fan

Even if your residence has air conditioning, dorm rooms get stuffy real fast, especially with two people and zero ventilation\. I bought a small clip\-on fan and it has been a lifesaver during warmer months and stuffy late\-night study sessions\.

## **What I didn’t really need\!**

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-5-940x627.png)

[Joonas Sild](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-pink-fan-sitting-on-top-of-a-table-ZBa8Jp411kY) Unsplash

### A printer

I was so sure I needed one but I used it like maybe three times all year? The Irving K\. Barber Learning Centre has printers you can use, and most assignments are submitted online anyway\. If you ever need help figuring out how the printers work, the CLC student staff are always around and happy to walk you through it\.

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/Untitled-design-edited.png)

[Pixelshot](https://www.canva.com/photos/MAG58GcRt7w-young-woman-cleaning-carpet-with-vacuum-cleaner-in-living-room/) Canva

### A vacuum cleaner

If you are in UBC housing, they actually lend out vacuums for free, so there is no reason to bring or buy your own\. Just check with your residence front desk\!

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-6-940x627.png)

[Clay Banks](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-pink-fan-sitting-on-top-of-a-table-ZBa8Jp411kY) Unsplash

### A monitor

Unless you are big into gaming or you genuinely study better at home all the time, you do not need to bring a monitor\. UBC libraries have monitors ranging from Mac to PC that you can use whenever you want, which saves you the hassle of fitting one onto your already\-tiny dorm desk\!

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-7-edited.png)

[Humphrey M](https://unsplash.com/photos/open-black-compact-refrigerator-filled-with-soda-bottles-3h7jbWXhpgM) Unsplash

### A mini fridge

This one really depends on your situation, but most UBC housing comes with a fridge after first year, and even in first year, you usually have access to a communal fridge on your floor\. A mini fridge takes up so much space and uses more power than you would think\. Try the communal one first, and then make a decision\!

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/image-9-940x529.png)

[Debby Hudson](https://unsplash.com/photos/three-assorted-decorative-bowls-in-white-surface-RXKERUSGN8U) Unsplash

### Cute food containers that are not microwave or dishwasher safe

Please check the bottom of your containers before buying\. I bought a whole set of cute ones that I could not microwave, which made meal prepping pointless when I had to transfer everything onto a plate first\. Get the boring, durable, microwave and dishwasher safe ones\.

---

What did you wish you had brought, or wish you had not? Drop your dorm essentials and regrets in the comments below\!

title: Top 10 Things I Wish I Knew Before Starting University
content_markdown:
When I first started at UBC, I genuinely thought I had it all figured out, and let me tell you, I really did not\. There are just so many small things that nobody warns you about\! So, here are ten things I wish someone had actually told me before my first week, rather than just the generic information every orientation video repeats\.

[Image](https://lc2023.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/vancouver-campus-looking-west_54142651638_o-edited-scaled.jpg)

### Nobody actually has it all figured out

Walking around campus in my first week, I genuinely believed everyone else had read the syllabus, planned their four\-year degree, and already made best friends\. Spoiler alert: they had not\. Almost everyone is just as lost and overwhelmed as you are; they are just better at hiding it\. The sooner I accepted that we were all winging it together, the less alone I felt\.

### Your professors actually want you to come to office hours

I avoided office hours my entire first semester because I was convinced I would be wasting their time\. The reality is that most professors are sitting alone, hoping someone will show up to talk to them about the course\. Going even once made my professor remember my name, and that genuinely helped when I needed a reference letter later or found summer internships in their department or even to TA their course\!

### The Chapman Learning Commons is a hidden gem

So much tech you can borrow, study spaces, computer stations, and student staff who genuinely want to help you figure things out\. I had no idea any of this existed until my second year, and I struggled alone for way too long before I found it\.

### AMS Health and Dental is opt\-out, not opt\-in

You are automatically enrolled and charged for it, and if you already have coverage through your parents or another plan, you can opt out and get a refund\. I did not know this for a full year and basically donated money for no reason\.

### Group projects will humble you

You will inevitably end up in a group with someone who disappears until the night before the deadline\. The best thing I learned was to set up a shared document early and assign roles in writing, so it is clear who is responsible for what\. It does not always prevent the chaos, but it gives you receipts and keeps you clear\-headed\.

### Vancouver weather requires a real raincoat

A cute jacket from a fast fashion store will not survive a Vancouver winter, and umbrellas are basically useless when the rain is sideways\. Invest in something properly waterproof with a hood, because you will be outside more than you expect, especially when running between classes\.

### The bus loop is a battlefield during exam season

Nobody tells you that the 99 B\-Line at 8:30 in the morning is basically a contact sport\. I started leaving 20 minutes earlier than I thought I needed to, and even then, I sometimes had to wait for two or three buses to pass before I could squeeze on\. If you commute, plan accordingly\.

### Joining six clubs in September is a trap

I signed up for everything at Imagine Day because I wanted to “make the most of university,” and by October, I was burnt out and ghosting all of them\. It is much better to commit to one or two things you actually care about than to spread yourself thin across clubs you will never attend\.

### The friends you make in first year might not be your friends forever

I felt so much pressure to lock in my friend group during the first month, and I held onto some friendships way longer than I should have because I was scared of being alone\. The truth is that people grow in different directions during university, and some of the best friendships I have now started in second or third year\.

### You are allowed to change literally everything

Your major, your friend group, your study spot, your routine, all of it is changeable\. I thought every decision I made in my first year was permanent, and that pressure made me miserable\. The people who seem the most put\-together are usually the ones who have changed their minds the most\.

---

What is something you wish you had known before starting university? Drop it in the comments below\!

title: How to Cite
content_markdown:
Citations, aka, *references* give credit to others for their work and ideas and allow readers to track down the original work if they choose\. The purpose of this guide is to help you identify the basic elements of a citation for some common types of materials\. You will find much more detailed instructions to formatting your references in the official guide for the style you are using\. Click the "Major Styles" tab and/or the "Using Style Guides" tab to learn more about finding and using style guides\. 

Whenever you use **someone else's words** or **ideas** in your paper or presentation, you must indicate that this information is borrowed by citing your source\. This applies to written sources you've used, such as books, articles and web pages, as well as other formats, such as images, sounds, TV/film clips, and DVDs\. Failure to cite such sources may be considered plagiarism\. Avoid distress and embarrassment by learning exactly what to cite – the **who**, **what**, **where** and **when** of your source\!

title: Library Skills Tutorial
content_markdown:
## About This Guide

This guide is an instructional resource intended to assist with access to basic UBC Library resources, with a focus on undergraduate students\.

Those with CWL affiliation \(students faculty and staff\) are highly encouraged to take the [UBC Library Skills Tutorials \(self\-enroll\)](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/F3GKXM)  and the [UBC Library Citation Tutorials \(self\-enroll\)](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/B7AYEN) courses for more tailored information\. 

Graduate students are encouraged to review subject\-specific [Research Guides](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/)\. Community and Alumni please see the [resources below](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/c.php?g=729610&p=5235763#s-lg-box-wrapper-19473044)\.

[Embedded content: YouTube video player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/Yr1zUs-bD9k?si=GHlJJce8yKyaqUad)

## Students: Get Started

**If you are a student at UBC, you will find tailored learning in the canvas course:** [Library Skills Tutorials \(self\-enroll\)](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/F3GKXM)

The course is designed to assist all users in becoming more familiar with UBC library\. It has 5 interactive modules with certificates awarded at completion of each module\. Modules are self\-paced and take between 15\-30 minutes each to complete\. Modules can be accessed in any order\. 

-   Module 1: Introduction to UBC Vancouver Library
-   Module 2: Exploring Sources
-   Module 3: Finding Sources \- Basic
-   Module 4: Finding Sources \- Advanced
-   Module 5: Evaluating Sources

## Instructors: Get Started

As instructors, faculty and staff can assign the [Library Skills Tutorials \(self\-enroll\)](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/F3GKXM), [Citation Tutorial \(self\-enroll\)](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/B7AYEN), or individual modules from each\. Options for grading completion for self\-enroll include: requiring students to submit PDF certificates \(generated upon each module's completion\) and/or other activity sheets provided in the modules as proof of completion\.

Instructors can also embed the modules in their courses\. This allows instructors to edit interactive materials such as assignments and quizzes\. [Embed Library Skills Tutorials from Canvas Commons](https://commons-yul-prod.instructure.com/resources/1b533018f69341d8bf73007bcc78c4b2?shared)\. [Embed Citation Tutorial from Canvas Commons](https://commons-yul-prod.instructure.com/resources/1b533018f69341d8bf73007bcc78c4b2?shared)\.

For more information contact the following librarians:

-   [Vancouver Campus: Learning Services Librarian, Lauren Lacey](mailto:lauren.lacey@ubc.ca)
-   [Okanagan Campus: Learning and Curriculum Support Librarian, Heather Berringer](mailto:heather.berringer@ubc.ca)

## Community and Alumni Users: Get Started

-   [Community Users Guide](https://services.library.ubc.ca/user-guides/community-users-visitors/#fragment-f8bd739ea18d6abc3fca164f72c80623-0)**:** Learn about library resources for community members, including maps, hours, and more\.
-   [Alumni Guide](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/alumniresources): Learn about library resources and access for alumni\. 
-   [How to Get a Library Card](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/library-cards/): For UBC students, staff, and faculty their UBC Card is their library card\. This link helps other users request a library card\.
-   [Connect to Library Resources](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/connect/):  This line helps users access UBC Library resources online\.
-   [Searching UBC Library](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/c.php?g=729610&p=5235765): Tips on how to use the search portal at the library\. This resource is designed for all users, for resources specific to students see the Canvas course linked above\. 
-   [Library Research Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXNVGMZWSlk&list=PLovTgrY9BSZEkwbuwh1Vebs0TeaY5xDk6): Visit our youtube playlist for a set of curated videos created by the library to help you research\. 

## Need Additional Assistance?

Visit us in person during [Library open hours](https://hours.library.ubc.ca/) or [Ask Us](https://ask.library.ubc.ca/) online\. 

Reach out to a [subject librarian](https://directory.library.ubc.ca/subjectlibrarians/) for more assistance\. 

See the 'Get Help' tab of this guide for more information\.
